blogs.title: When Expert Testimony Breaks the Law: The Case of Dr. Wells and the Failure of ‘Signals of Interest’
blogs.description: This post dissects the appellate court’s analysis of Finesse Wireless’s expert testimony in the ’134 patent infringement claim. It examines how the court determined that Dr. Wells’ contradictory and incomplete mapping of signal paths rendered the jury’s verdict unsupported by substantial evidence, addressing the broader implications for expert testimony standards and the burden of proof in technology‑intensive patent cases.

blogs.title: Claim Construction in the Digital Domain: ‘Three Signals’ vs. ‘Two or Three Signals’ in the ’775 Patent
blogs.description: Focusing on the ’775 patent, this article explores the appellate court’s nuanced discussion of claim scope and the doctrine of claim disavowal. It clarifies how the court concluded that Finesse did not surrender claim territory over the number of unique inputs and how the failure to demonstrate the seven required multiplications collapsed the infringement analysis.

blogs.title: Damages Frozen by Infringement Uncertainty: A Wake‑up Call for Patent Litigation Damages Calculations
blogs.description: This piece analyzes the court’s decision to vacate the enormous lump‑sum damages award following the reversed JMOL. It explains the standard for new trial and JMOL on damages, the influence of substantial‑evidence findings, and what this means for how damages are calculated, disputed, and potentially overturned when infringement is not firmly established.

blogs.title: The Fifth Circuit’s Two‑Step Standard for JMOL in Patent Litigation: Lessons from Finesse Wireless
blogs.description: Examining the appellate court’s application of the Fifth Circuit’s de novo review of JMOL and the substantial‑evidence standard, this post shows how a failure to support jury findings on both factual and interpretive grounds can lead to reversal. It highlights the doctrinal importance of the receptive evidence rule and the impact on future appeals in the telecommunications sector.
